body:
Pyro,
	Dr. Pierce wrote a lucid essay in 1971 titled "Man and Technology."
He was responding to the views of someone who proposed to escape into the
wilderness rather than face the issues presented by technology 
--like you, he argues that technology also poses dangers to the social and
moral fabric of our country.  He urged that those who would turn trees into
plastic be removed from our midst.  The essay was followed by bomb-making
instructions.  The symbol of the National Alliance, the Yggdrasil, was
explained in that newsletter, as it was explained in every subsequent issue. 
The symbol signifies rebirth and renewal and was chosen, in part, because it is
easily spraypainted on buildings.  A Professor Hill spotted a symbol -- which
by his description was the Yggdrasil (an inverted peace sign in a circle) --
painted on the library shortly before the bombings of Professors Gelernter and
Epstein.  

p.s.  Why bother concern yourself
with eugenics?  What's the point?
Aren't such considerations largely irrelevant from the point of view of policy?
 Equal rights are predicated on a moral principle that does not need to
presuppose equal ability.
p.s.s.  How much of Dr. Pierce's works have you read?  Have you also read
"Hunter"?  (Am I right that you've read "Turner Diaries"?)  I find his early
work especially revealing, as when he did the ghost writing for George Lincoln
Rockwell in Pierce's early days.  
p.s.s.s.  What's your source on the prize you mention?
p.s.s.s.s.  In an interview with a German doctoral student from Berlin, Dr.
Pierce says that TK represents the new prototype of a revolutionary.  Note that
TK and Pierce disagree fundamentally (paras. 222, 227, and 229), in which TK
muses how to harness the energies of the True Believer to his hoped-for
revolution.
p.s.s.s.s.  Do you know the ever-articulate Milton K., whose rhetoric was as
incendiary as yours.  He had a falling out with Pierce because Pierce would use
technology in connection with eugenics.  (That was Pierce's point in 1971, that
even though the guys with the funny noses were responsible largely for
technology and declining moral values, technology could be useful in promoting
certain aims).
p.s.s.s.s.s.  The FBI has not disclosed the name of the other organizations
that TK has corresponded with.  Key pages of David's FBI interviews are still
redacted (beginning after a comment about the militia-type groups that TK may
have associated with in the past).
p.s.s.s.s.s.t.  Did you know that the good doctor was a secret member of Robert
Mathews' group "The Order" -- his codename was Cookie.   In his advanced age,
though, I think he's given up his more adventurous romantic activities and
focused on his mail order sales and other sources of revenue.
